_comment: Daily map events (PLAN.md). Hours are game hours (divided by world speed). Every `everyHours` from the start of a run (the first after its first day), an event rises on passable open land `range.min` to `range.max` hexes from one of the players' villages, and goes after `lastsHours` unless an army is already on its way to it. `kinds` are picked by weight. captives: a camp (kind 'captives') of `guards` of the land's front, more each day (x 1 + `growthPerDay` x (day - 1)), holding captives: freeing them (clearing the camp) brings, with chance `unitsChance`, `count` (+ `countPerDay` a day) of one of `units` into the army that freed them, or else `resources` (x 1 + `growthPerDay` x (day - 1)) carried home with it; it doesn't grow, join hordes or ambush caravans. ruin: a hard ancient site (sites.json) watched by `guardianFactor` times its usual guardians, whose resources are worth `lootFactor` times as much. shipyard: a group project on a river bank (a hex beside a river edge), never on a river (or a lake it reaches) that already has a shipyard, open, building or done: any player sends resources from a village within `range` hexes until `cost` is paid (if nobody has sent anything when its time is up, it goes); then the boat takes `buildHours` to build, and every `raidEveryHours` raiders (`raiders` of the land's front, more each day like the captives' guards) strike it in `raiderStance`: armies standing on its hex defend it one after another, and if they don't drive them off, `setbackHours` of work are lost; burned `maxBurns` times, the shipyard is lost and the event fails. When the boat is done, armies, caravans and scouts stepping between two hexes beside that river (every river edge joined to the one it was built on) move `laneSpeed` times as fast, for good; a lake the river reaches is sailed too (its hexes, at a move cost of `lakeMoveCost` before the lane's speed, its shores, and the rivers flowing into it join the lane), though no army can stop on a lake. ritual (rare): cultists of Černobog camp (`guards` of the land's front, more each day like the captives' guards) and work a ritual that ends `hours` game hours after it begins; every soldier of yours who falls fighting them brings it `minutesPerFallen` game minutes closer. Clearing the camp stops it, for the event's bounty. If it ends, the Avatar of Černobog (`avatar`, enemies.json, a single foe as strong as a great horde) rises where they stood and marches on the villages like a horde, of the camp's front; slaying it brings `avatarBountyFactor` times the bounty to every member. Every event done brings a bounty, `reward.resources` (x 1 + `reward.growthPerDay` x (day of the run - 1)), to the first village of whoever did it (captives freed, a ruin searched); a finished boat brings it to every member. An event left undone when its time is up (captives taken away, a ruin nobody searched, a shipyard nobody paid into) makes the next horde of its front (the land it rose in, or the first active one) hate the more: `failure.hatred` added to its hatred (horde.json). Each is told to the players as an event notice, which the game shows in a popup. mountain_city (rare): a neutral city rises in a mountain (a mountain hex beside passable land, as a shipyard rises on a bank): the hex becomes Mountain City land that armies can enter and hold. It is paid for and defended like a shipyard: any player sends `cost` from a village within `range` hexes (or by caravan); then the city takes `buildHours` to build, and every `raidEveryHours` monsters from under the mountain (`raiders` of the `raiderFront`'s monsters, more each day like the captives' guards) strike it in `raiderStance`: armies standing on its hex defend it, and if they don't drive them off, `setbackHours` of work are lost; struck down `maxBurns` times, the city is lost, the event fails and the hex is mountain again (as it is if nobody pays before the event ends). Once built it stands for good, and every member's villages produce `productionBonus` more of every resource (each city adds its own), with the bounty to every member. A built city trades: a caravan that brings it grain brings back `stonePerGrain` stone for each. It is also a neutral supply point (any player's caravans fill its grain store, any army standing there draws on it); hordes never come into the mountains, so none burns it, and no bandits take it.
